faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's net banking portal using the ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility, or through your stockbroker's platform. You will need a demat account and a trading account.
A lot size is the minimum number of shares you must apply for in an IPO. You cannot apply for fewer shares than the specified lot size, and you must apply in multiples of that lot size.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies that list on the main exchanges (NSE and BSE). SME (Small and Medium Enterprises) IPOs are for smaller companies and are listed on dedicated SME platforms of the exchanges (like NSE Emerge or BSE SME). SME IPOs often have higher lot sizes and different regulatory requirements.

faq.q: Can I sell my shares on the first day of listing?
faq.a: Yes, if you are allotted shares in an IPO, you can sell them on the very first day they are listed on the stock exchange.

faq.q: What happens if I don't get an allotment?
faq.a: If you don't receive any shares in the allotment process, the money that was blocked in your bank account for the IPO application will be unblocked and released back to you.
